name: equal-length paths are broken by walking back to the smallest neighbour
why: s and t are opposite corners of the undirected 6-cycle s-a-y-t-b-z. Forward breadth-first search would discover t from y first (a is dequeued before z) and return s, a, y, t; the rule instead walks back from t to the smallest-ID neighbour one hop closer, which is b, then z. The rule is easy to state in any language.

queries.why: t's neighbours b and y are both 2 from s; b is smaller. b's only neighbour at distance 1 is z.
Reversed: s's neighbours a and z are both 2 from t; a is smaller. So paths are not simply reversed.
q is isolated. No path is a different answer from an empty path.
Opposite corners of the 6-cycle are 3 apart: (a,b), (s,t), (y,z). The isolated q is skipped, not infinitely far. (a,b) is the smallest pair.
